title: Thresholded concurrency hedging to stabilize initial-token latency across multi-variant workloads
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Several enterprise customers across Hosted and Dedicated reported intermittent 200-600ms TTFT spikes and tokens/sec drop when model-variant fanout and tenant concurrency peak simultaneously. Investigation shows contention at the serving queue boundary combined with aggressive worker multiplexing: short-lived, high-priority requests preempt kernel scheduling and force warmstart/eviction churn for other inflight streams. Result: first-token latency spikes and sustained throughput collapse for some tenants and private deployments. This ticket implements a defensible, low-risk hedging layer that thresholds concurrency per tenant/model-variant and issues polite hedged requests (soft duplicate to warm pool) to avoid blocking kernel scheduling and reduce eviction storms. The goal is to regain median TTFT and stabilize tokens/sec within SLA while preserving throughput for bulk workloads.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use multi-variant load generator with 10 tenants and mixed short/long prompt mix (90% short <50 tokens, 10% long >512 tokens).
2) Ramp concurrency per tenant to 4x normal across 30s window while toggling simultaneous model-variant fanout (spawn both quantized int8 and fp16 variants).
3) Observe first-byte/first-token latency histograms and token/sec drop on the affected worker pools during fanout transitions.
4) Reproduce in Dedicated by running same workload pinned to single GPU pool to validate private/VPC behavior.
proposed_solution: Implement a thresholded concurrency controller per tenant+model-variant that enforces a soft cap and queuing policy when transient bursts exceed a configurable window.
Add hedged warmstart: for short requests that would block the main execution path, issue a low-cost speculative wake to an idle warm worker (cancel if main path wins).
Introduce a lightweight eviction backpressure signal from the kernel scheduler to the hedging controller so hedges reduce when eviction rate increases.
Expose mitigation knobs in Dedicated config and Private operator manifest (max_hedge_ratio, burst_window_ms, per_tenant_cap).
rollout_plan: 1) Feature branch + unit tests (runtime hedging controller) and e2e test harness using load-generator scenario — target MR: runtime#4587.
2) Canary rollout to Hosted region us-west-2: enable hedging for 5% of traffic with telemetry flags for eviction_rate and ttft_95/99.
3) Expand to Dedicated pools with a single customer pilot (opt-in) and monitor for any throughput regressions for long-form workloads.
4) Full rollout to Hosted and toggle on by default for Dedicated/Private in the next minor runtime release after validation.
5) If regressions observed, automatic rollback via feature-flag and emergency-runbook to revert to previous scheduler config.
monitoring_and_metrics: Primary metrics: ttft_median, ttft_p95, tokens_per_sec_per_pool, eviction_rate, kernel_preempt_count
Dashboards: add an "hedging" panel to runtime / serving-dashboard with tenant heatmap and model-variant breakdown
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: poorly tuned hedging could increase overall work and reduce throughput for long requests. Mitigation: conservative default max_hedge_ratio=0.15 and auto-throttle via eviction signal.
Risk: unexpected interactions with existing prefetch/KV caching. Mitigation: run combined load tests with kv_prefetch enabled and observe cache hit ratios; disable hedging if hit ratio drop >5%.
Risk: private deployments may have operator-managed constraints. Mitigation: make hedging opt-in in private release and provide clear operator docs and knobs.
customer_notes: Customer A (enterprise fintech) reported recurring 400ms+ TTFT spikes during end-of-day batch queries — offered pilot with per-tenant cap and saw 62% p95 improvement in pilot pool.
Customer B (healthcare) experienced tokens/sec sag during multi-variant A/B rollouts; they will join the Dedicated pilot and help validate operator controls.
Support runbook updated: steps to toggle hedging feature-flag and verify kernel eviction metrics (link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/incident/hedging-runbook)
Escalation channel: pagerduty#prod-inference and shared Slack #prod-ttft.
